unit.title: Coordinate and manage basic installation projects

theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: What should a project coordinator have in hand before work starts on a small shop installation?
options: A signed scope, price and drawings
All of the materials stacked on the site
A full team waiting at the gate each day
The power company's meter already fitted

questions.stem: On a small installation project, what is the coordinator's main job?
options: To do all of the wiring work personally
To bring people, materials and work together on time
To keep the client away from the site at all times
To check the final bill and nothing else

questions.stem: The plumber and the electricians both want to run services through the same ceiling space on the same day. What should the coordinator do?
options: Let the two trades sort it out on the day
Send both trades home until next week
Agree routes and times with both beforehand
Let whichever trade arrives first take the space

questions.stem: On a new house, when is the electrical work normally done in relation to the other trades?
options: All wiring after the painters have finished
First fix before plastering; second fix after it and painting
Second fix before plastering; first fix after painting
All wiring before the block walls are built

questions.stem: In Jamaica, which step comes just before the power company energises the supply to a newly wired building?
options: The client pays the electrical contractor in full
The neighbours sign a letter agreeing to the work
The painter signs off the walls as finished
The installation passes the government inspection

questions.stem: What is a 'milestone' in a project programme?
options: A key event with a date, such as 'first fix complete'
The distance by road from the store to the site
Any single task that takes longer than one week
A heavy item that needs two or more people to lift it

questions.stem: Two jobs both need the firm's only cable-pulling winch on the same day. What should the coordinator do?
options: Let the first team that reaches the store take it
Reschedule one job's pull or hire a second winch
Tell one team to pull the heavy cable by hand
Cancel the work on both jobs for that day

questions.stem: Who should the coordinator choose to terminate and test the new distribution board?
options: The newest trainee, working alone to learn
Whoever finishes their other task first
A competent electrician, with a trainee helping
The labourer, since the board is already fixed

questions.stem: The client's staff keep walking through the area where floor boxes are being fitted. What should the coordinator do?
options: Ask the team to work faster and finish early
Let them pass, since it is their own building
Stop the work for the rest of the project
Put up barriers and signs, and agree access

questions.stem: Part of a working office must be isolated so new circuits can be connected. Why must the coordinator agree the shutdown time with the client?
options: So the client can plan for staff and computers
So the client can watch the electricians at work
So the power company can read the meter
So the work can be done live if it runs late

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of a short site meeting at the start of each week?
options: To hand out the workers' pay slips for the week
To let the client choose new paint colours
To agree the week's tasks, problems and owners
To decide which worker will drive the van

questions.stem: Why should the coordinator keep a daily site diary?
options: To log progress, visitors, delays and instructions
To keep private notes about each member of the team
To list the phone numbers of all the suppliers
To plan the company's end-of-year party

questions.stem: Halfway through the job, the client asks for six extra outlets. What should the coordinator do before the team fits them?
options: Fit them at once to keep the client happy
Agree the extra cost and time in writing
Refuse, because they are not on the drawing
Fit them and add them to the bill quietly

questions.stem: First fix is 60% complete, but the team has used 80% of the hours planned for it. What does this tell the coordinator?
options: The job is ahead of time and under its labour cost
The job is exactly on track with its plan
The job is likely to go over its labour budget
The hours for first fix were planned too high

questions.stem: Three electricians each work 8 hours a day for 4 days. How many labour hours have been used?
options: 32 hours
72 hours
96 hours
120 hours

questions.stem: The light fittings will arrive a week late. What should the coordinator do first?
options: Stop the whole job until the fittings arrive
Tell the team to take a week of leave
Buy any light fittings at all from a nearby shop
Re-plan so that other tasks go ahead meanwhile

questions.stem: Which risk should the coordinator plan for on an outdoor job in the rainy season?
options: The van using more fuel when parked in the hot sun
The client asking for fewer outlets
Hand tools becoming lighter when wet
Rain delaying trenching and outdoor work

questions.stem: A subcontractor will dig a trench for an underground cable. What should the coordinator check before digging starts?
options: Where buried services are, and that the digger is competent
That the subcontractor has bought a brand-new shovel
That the cable is already lying in the trench
That the client has finished painting the front wall

questions.stem: Why should the coordinator plan internal inspections at stages, not only at the end?
options: So the team has more paperwork to complete
So faults are found while easy to fix
So the job takes longer and earns more money
So the client has something to do each week

questions.stem: The job is finished and passed. Which papers go to the client in the handover pack?
options: The supplier's invoices and delivery notes
The team's timesheets and pay records
Test results, as-built drawings and manuals
The firm's price list for next year's maintenance work

questions.stem: What is a 'snag list' (punch list)?
options: Small items to finish before handover
The list of workers who arrived late on site
The full list of materials still to be bought
The list of tools that need to be repaired

questions.stem: Why does a coordinator hold a short review meeting after a project ends?
options: To find one person to blame for the problems
To share out the left-over materials
To agree the firm's next price rise
To learn what went well and what to improve

questions.stem: Materials have cost J$420 000 against a budget of J$400 000. By what percentage is the job over its materials budget?
Who should give the team instructions on site about changes to the work?
options: Anyone at all from the client's office
The coordinator, after agreeing them with the client
The security guard on duty at the gate
The first worker who hears about the change

questions.stem: Before work starts on a factory roof, the client requires a 'permit to work'. What is this?
options: A written approval setting the safe conditions for the work
A licence that allows a firm to sell electrical goods in shops
A pass that lets the team use the factory canteen
A paper that allows electricians to work on live parts

questions.stem: What is a 'toolbox talk' on an installation site?
options: A list of the tools that are kept in the van
A talk with the supplier about tool prices
A short talk on site about the day's hazards
A meeting held to choose which tools to buy

questions.stem: The client asks how the job is going. Which reply is the best progress report?
options: Going well, we are nearly finished
Rooms 1–3 first fixed; room 4 due Friday
Some problems, but we will manage
Ask the workers, they will know

questions.stem: A new building needs the power company to provide a service and meter. When should the coordinator start this?
options: Early, because it needs notice and paperwork
On the day the client first wants power
Only after the client has moved into the building
Never, because the electrician fits the meter

questions.stem: One electrician has three tasks for the same morning while another has none. What is the coordinator's best action?
options: Leave it, because the busy one will cope
Give the idle one the afternoon off
Ask the client to choose who does what
Share out the tasks to balance the work

questions.stem: A worker reports a near miss: a ladder slipped on a tiled floor. What should the coordinator do?
options: Tell the worker to be more careful next time
Record it, find the cause and fix it first
Ignore it, because nobody was hurt
Move the ladder into another room

questions.stem: Who is responsible for planning how cable offcuts and packaging are removed from site?
options: The coordinator, as part of the project plan
The client's office cleaner at the end of the day
The power company, when it fits the meter
Nobody; it is left for whichever trade comes next

questions.stem: The architect issues revision C of the floor plan. What must the coordinator do?
options: Keep using revision B until the job ends
Use whichever revision is easier to read
Issue revision C and remove old copies
File revision C in the office unread

questions.stem: Why should a project programme include time for the government electrical inspection?
options: The inspector needs a week to travel to the site
The inspector does part of the wiring on the job
So the team can take a rest while waiting
Supply cannot be connected until it is passed

questions.stem: A subcontractor's cable trench is shallower than the drawing shows. What should the coordinator do?
options: Accept it, to save time on the job programme
Have it corrected before the cable is laid
Lay the cable and backfill it quickly
Change the drawing to match the trench

questions.stem: Why should the coordinator give each team member a written job card?
options: So each knows the task, place, materials and hazards
So nobody needs to ask the coordinator any questions
So the client can pay each worker directly
So the job card can be used later as a receipt

questions.stem: A worker gets a serious electric shock from a cable that another trade has damaged. What is the first action?
options: Pull the worker away using your bare hands
Switch off the supply, then give first aid and call help
Finish the task, then call the coordinator
Pour water over the cable to cool it down

questions.stem: What is the best way to confirm an instruction that the client gave by phone?
options: Remember it until the end of the job
Tell the team and hope they remember
Send a short written message and keep a copy
Wait until the client repeats it on site

questions.stem: Why are timesheets checked against the programme each week?
options: To compare the hours used with the hours planned
To see who is wearing the company shirt
To decide which colour the next company van should be
To check that home addresses are up to date

questions.stem: At handover, why should the coordinator show the client how to use the main switch and test the GFCI outlets?
options: So the client can do their own wiring later on
So the client will not need any warranty
So the client can take out the breakers
So the client can isolate in an emergency and check protection

questions.stem: The air-conditioning installer needs a 220 V supply point beside each indoor unit. When should the positions be agreed?
options: After the walls have been painted
At planning, and marked on the drawing
When the A/C units are first switched on
When the client complains that they are missing

questions.stem: Which should be in place on the first day of setting up a site?
options: First-aid kit, fire extinguisher and a lockable store
The final test certificate for the whole installation
The client's new furniture in every room
The as-built drawings for the finished job

questions.stem: Who is a 'stakeholder' in a small installation project?
options: Only the person who owns the building
Only the workers who are on the site
Anyone affected by or involved in the project
Only the firm that supplies the cable

questions.stem: The coordinator finds switches fitted at 1.0 m instead of the 1.2 m on the drawing. What is the best step?
options: Leave them, as they still work properly
Change the drawing to 1.0 m without asking
Wait to see if the inspector notices them
Correct them and find out why it happened

questions.stem: A task needs 48 person-hours. Two electricians each work 8 hours a day on it. How many days will it take?
options: 2 days
3 days
4 days
6 days

questions.stem: What should happen to unused materials at the end of a project?
options: Thrown in the skip with the waste
Taken home by the workers
Recorded and returned to store or client
Left lying on site with no record

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: What are the drawings called that show the installation as it was finally built, with all changes?
A task needs 36 person-hours. Three workers do it together. How many hours does it take?
What is a change to the agreed work, such as extra outlets, that alters the price or time usually called?
The budget is J$250 000 and J$190 000 has been spent. How much is left, in J$?
A job starts on Monday 2 March and lasts 10 working days (Monday to Friday only). On what date does it finish?
What is the name for the timed list of all the project's tasks with their start and finish dates?
What one word is used for passing the finished work over to the client?
What is the term for the sum kept aside in a project budget to cover unexpected costs?
Four electricians each work 40 hours in a week at J$1 500 an hour. What is the week's labour cost, in J$?
What is the name for a firm hired by the main contractor to do part of the work, such as trenching?
What two-word term is used for an event that almost caused an injury or damage, but did not?
A project planned for 20 days is now 5 days late. By what percentage has it overrun?
What is the written record of who attended a meeting, what was decided and who will act called?
On a programme, what is the chain of linked tasks that sets the shortest possible time for the whole job called?
A job is run by 2 electricians and 1 helper. A second job the same size starts with the same team size. How many people are needed for both jobs?

essays.stem: You are coordinating the electrical installation of a small two-storey shop in Mandeville. Describe how you would set up the project in the first week.
essays.modelAnswer: I would first make sure the scope, price, drawings and specification are agreed and signed with the client, and that I have the latest revision of each drawing. I would walk the site with the main contractor to see access, storage, power for tools and hazards. I would prepare a programme with milestones, linked to the builder's programme, and plan the team and the materials for each stage, ordering long-lead items such as the board early. I would set up the site: a lockable store, first-aid kit, fire extinguisher, signs and a place for waste. I would hold a start meeting with the client and the other trades to agree how we will communicate, who gives instructions and how changes are approved. I would start the site diary and give the team a toolbox talk, job cards and the risk assessment before any work begins.
markingPoints: Signed scope, price and current drawings
Site walk: access, storage, hazards
Programme with milestones linked to the builder; resources and long-lead orders
Site set-up: store, first aid, extinguisher, signs, waste
Start meeting, communication rules, diary, toolbox talk and job cards

essays.stem: Explain how you would coordinate the electrical work with the masons, plumbers, carpenters and painters on a new house.
essays.modelAnswer: I would get the builder's programme and fit our stages into it. Conduit and boxes in block walls must go in as the masons build or before they plaster, so I would agree those dates with the mason and have the work inspected before plastering. I would meet the plumber to agree routes in the ceiling and walls, keeping cables away from hot pipes and water. I would tell the carpenter where cable drops and fittings go before ceilings are closed, and make sure our first fix in the roof is done and checked first. Second fix would follow the plaster and the first coat of paint, agreed with the painter, so accessories are not painted over. I would attend the site meetings, share our drawings and confirm changes in writing. Any clash would be raised early and solved with the builder.
markingPoints: Fits electrical stages into the builder's programme
First fix in walls agreed with the mason and inspected before plaster
Routes agreed with the plumber; carpenter told before ceilings close
Second fix timed with the painter
Attends meetings, shares drawings, confirms changes and solves clashes early

essays.stem: Describe how you would monitor progress and cost on a ten-week project, and what you would do if the job fell behind.
essays.modelAnswer: Each day I would record in the site diary what was done, who was on site and any problems. Each week I would compare the work done with the programme, for example the percentage of first fix complete, and compare the hours used and the materials bought with the budget for each stage. I would mark progress on the bar chart so everyone can see it. If the job fell behind, I would find the cause first: late materials, too few people, rework or waiting for another trade. Then I would decide what to do, such as changing the order of tasks, adding a person, working an agreed extra shift, or chasing the supplier. I would tell my manager and the client early, with the reason and a new forecast date. I would keep safety and quality checks in place even when trying to catch up.
markingPoints: Daily site diary records
Weekly comparison of progress, hours and materials against the plan and budget
Finds the cause of the delay
Takes action: re-order tasks, add resources, chase suppliers
Reports early with a new forecast; does not cut safety or quality

essays.stem: The client asks for changes halfway through a project. Explain how you would handle the change from the request to the finished work.
essays.modelAnswer: I would listen to the request and write down exactly what the client wants, for example six more outlets and a new outside light. I would check the effect on the design: the load, the cable sizes, the board space and the drawings. I would work out the extra materials, labour hours, cost and time, and any effect on other trades or the inspection date. I would give the client a written variation with the price and the new finish date, and wait for written approval before the team starts. Once approved, I would update the drawings, order the materials, change the programme and brief the team with new job cards. When the extra work is done it is inspected and tested like the rest, recorded on the as-built drawings and added to the final account.
markingPoints: Records exactly what is asked
Checks the design effects: load, cables, board, drawings
Prices the extra cost and time and gives a written variation
Starts only after written approval; updates drawings, orders and programme; briefs the team
Inspects and tests, records on as-builts and final account

essays.stem: Explain how you would plan and manage a shutdown of part of a working office so that new circuits can be connected safely.
essays.modelAnswer: I would meet the client to agree the date and time, such as a Saturday, and how long the power will be off, so they can protect computers, data and staff. I would identify exactly which circuits and boards are affected from the drawings and a survey. I would prepare the new work beforehand so the shutdown is as short as possible, and have all materials and tools ready. On the day I would brief the team on the method and hazards. The circuits would be safely isolated: switched off, locked off with each worker's own lock, tagged, and proved dead with a voltage indicator checked on a proving unit before and after. Nobody works live. After the connections are made, they are inspected and tested dead, locks are removed only when everyone is clear, and the supply is restored by the authorised person. I would then confirm with the client that everything is working.
markingPoints: Agrees date, time and length with the client
Identifies the affected circuits and prepares work beforehand
Briefs the team
Safe isolation: off, lock, tag, prove dead with checked tester; no live work
Tests before restoring, removes locks when all clear, authorised person restores and checks with client

essays.stem: Describe the safety arrangements a coordinator should put in place and check on a small installation site.
essays.modelAnswer: Before work starts I would make sure there is a risk assessment and method statement for each main task, and that the team has read them. I would give a site induction and regular toolbox talks. I would provide first aid, a fire extinguisher and a clear emergency plan, with the nearest hospital known. I would make sure everyone has and wears the right PPE. Ladders, steps and towers would be checked before use. Safe isolation would be the rule for every circuit: switch off, lock off, tag and prove dead with a tester checked before and after, and no live work. Work areas would be barriered and signed to keep the client's staff and the public away. I would check housekeeping daily so cables and offcuts are not trip hazards. Accidents and near misses would be reported, recorded and acted on.
markingPoints: Risk assessments and method statements read by the team
Induction, toolbox talks, first aid, extinguisher and emergency plan
PPE and access equipment checked
Safe isolation for every circuit, no live work
Barriers, housekeeping, and reporting of accidents and near misses

essays.stem: Explain how you would prepare for the government electrical inspection and the connection of supply by the power company.
essays.modelAnswer: Early in the project I would find out what the inspection and the power company need, and start any applications so their lead times do not delay the job. As the work goes on, I would make sure our own inspections are done at each stage, especially before walls and ceilings are closed. Near the end I would complete our own full inspection and dead tests, fix every defect and record the results. I would prepare the documents the inspector expects, such as the drawings and test results, and make sure the board is labelled, covers are fitted and the earthing is complete. I would book the inspection date in the programme and be there with a competent electrician to answer questions. If the inspector finds defects, we correct them promptly and arrange a re-inspection. Once passed, I would arrange the connection with the power company and plan who will be present.
markingPoints: Finds out the requirements early and starts applications
Own stage inspections during the work
Full own inspection and dead tests, defects fixed and recorded
Documents, labels, covers and earthing ready; inspection booked and attended
Corrects any defects and then arranges connection by the power company

essays.stem: Describe what should happen at the handover of a finished installation, and what the client should receive.
essays.modelAnswer: Before handover I would walk the job with the team and make a snag list of anything not finished, and get it all done. I would make sure the work is inspected, tested and passed, and the site is clean, with waste and unused materials removed. At the handover meeting I would walk the client round the installation. I would show them the main switch, how to isolate in an emergency, how to reset a breaker and how to test the GFCI outlets. I would explain any special equipment. The client should receive the test results and certificate, the as-built drawings, an up-to-date circuit chart in the board, the makers' manuals and warranties, and our contact details for problems. I would ask the client to sign that they have received the work and the documents, and tell them the warranty period.
markingPoints: Snag list completed before handover
Work inspected, tested and passed; site clean
Shows the client the main switch, isolation, breaker reset and GFCI test
Hands over test results, as-builts, circuit chart, manuals and warranties
Gets a signed acceptance and explains the warranty and contact details

essays.stem: Explain how good communication with the client and the team helps a project succeed. Give examples of the methods you would use.
essays.modelAnswer: Good communication means everyone knows what is to be done, by when, and what has changed. It prevents mistakes, delays, arguments and accidents. With the client, I would agree one contact person each, give a short weekly progress report, and confirm every instruction or change in writing by email or message, keeping a copy. I would warn the client early about shutdowns, delays or extra costs. With the team, I would hold a short briefing each morning and a weekly site meeting, use job cards so each person knows the task, location and hazards, and keep up-to-date drawings on site. I would listen to the team's problems and ideas. I would keep minutes of meetings and a site diary so there is a record. For example, a written variation stops arguments about extra outlets at the final bill.
markingPoints: Explains why: prevents mistakes, delays, disputes and accidents
Client: one contact, weekly reports, written confirmation, early warnings
Team: daily briefings, site meetings, job cards, current drawings
Records: minutes and site diary
Gives a clear example

essays.stem: After a project ends, explain how you would review it and use what you learn on the next job.
essays.modelAnswer: Soon after handover I would gather the facts: the planned and actual times for each stage, the budget and actual costs, the defects found at inspection, any accidents or near misses, and the client's feedback. I would hold a short review meeting with the team and ask what went well, what went badly and why. For example, we may find that first fix took longer because materials arrived late, or that labelling errors caused a re-inspection. I would write down the main lessons and agree actions, such as ordering certain items earlier, adding a check to the checklist, or more training on a task. I would update our estimating figures with the real times so future prices are more accurate. I would share the lessons with the manager and make sure they are used when the next project is planned.
markingPoints: Collects facts: times, costs, defects, safety, client feedback
Holds a review meeting with the team
Finds causes of what went well and badly
Writes lessons and agreed actions; updates estimating figures
Shares lessons and uses them on the next job

practical1.title: Set up a project plan and run the start-up meeting for a small installation
practical1.brief: The assessor gives the group a job pack for a small installation: drawings for a two-storey shop, the client's requirements, the builder's programme, supplier lead times, a labour rate and a budget. As a project team, prepare a project file: (1) the agreed scope with a list of what is not included; (2) a programme with milestones, linked to the builder's programme, including the government inspection and the power company connection; (3) a resource plan for people, tools and materials, with order dates; (4) a trade coordination plan showing when the masons, plumber, carpenter and painter need the electrical team; (5) a risk register with controls, including safe isolation and public safety; (6) a communication plan and a variation form. Then hold a role-played start-up meeting: one member chairs, and the others present their parts to the assessor, who plays the client and the builder. One member writes the minutes. Each member leads one part of the file and checks another member's part. Photograph each stage and hand in the file.
materials: Job pack from the assessor: drawings, client requirements, builder's programme, lead times, labour rate and budget
Blank forms: programme sheet, resource plan, risk register, variation form, minutes sheet
Flip chart, markers and sticky notes
Graph paper or a computer with a spreadsheet
Calculators, scale rules, pens and a phone or camera for photos
photos: The resource plan with order dates
The risk register and variation form
The signed minutes of the meeting
checklist: Led one part of the project file and made it complete and accurate
Linked the electrical stages correctly to the builder's programme and other trades
Included the inspection, the power company connection and long-lead items in the programme
Included safe isolation (lock, tag, prove dead with a tester checked before and after) and public safety in the risk register
Presented their part clearly and answered the client's questions
Checked another member's part and corrected errors
Took part in agreeing actions recorded in the minutes
safety: This is a planning task: no tools or supplies are used
Plan every task so that no work is done live
Keep the room tidy, with bags and laptop cables off the floor
Follow the Centre's rules for the classroom

practical2.title: Coordinate a staged installation on training bays and hand it over
practical2.brief: The group runs a small installation as a mini-project on two of the Centre's training bays: a lighting circuit and a socket circuit from a small training board, wired dead and never connected to a supply. The assessor gives the drawing, a short programme and the materials. Each member acts as coordinator for one stage (set-up, first fix, wiring, second fix, inspection and handover) and the others work under them. The coordinator for each stage gives a short briefing, issues job cards, records progress in the site diary and checks the stage before it is signed off. Halfway through, the assessor (as the client) asks for a change: one extra outlet. The group must price it with a variation form, get written approval and fit it. At the end the group carries out safe isolation and a visual inspection and dead tests, completes a snag list and fixes it, marks up an as-built drawing and hands over to the assessor with a short walk-round. Only the instructor may energise anything. Photograph each stage.
materials: Two training bays with a small training board (not connected to any supply)
Cable, conduit or trunking, boxes, switches, socket outlets and lampholders as the drawing lists
Hand tools, insulated screwdrivers, drill and fixings
Lock-off kit, danger tags, voltage indicator and proving unit
Low-resistance ohmmeter or multifunction tester in calibration
Job cards, site diary, variation form, snag list and an as-built drawing sheet
photos: The stage briefing and job cards
First fix complete before it is signed off
The variation form with the client's approval
The training board locked off and tagged, and the tester being checked
The snag list and the corrected items
The as-built drawing and the handover walk-round
checklist: As stage coordinator, briefed the team clearly and issued job cards
Recorded progress and problems in the site diary
Handled the variation correctly: priced, approved in writing, then fitted
Worked safely and neatly to the drawing in the other stages
Carried out safe isolation correctly before inspection and testing
Completed the snag list and as-built drawing accurately
Explained the installation clearly at the handover
safety: The training bays are never connected to a supply; only the instructor energises anything
Prove dead with a tester checked on a proving unit before and after, with each member's own lock and tag
Wear safety glasses when drilling and cutting, and use insulated tools in good condition
Keep cables, offcuts and tools off the floor to prevent trips
Use steps safely, with one person holding them when work is above head height
